mainTopic: Blood placed in the wrong spot on the מזבח: when it can create פיגול, and how ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן and שמואל explain the משנה's ruling.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about wrong intentions while offering a קרבן. Intent for 'outside its place' makes the קרבן פסול, while intent for 'outside its time' makes it פיגול with כרת. Intent to sprinkle the blood in the wrong spot on the next day makes it only פסול. The גמרא asks why it is not פיגול, if blood placed in the wrong spot counts as placed in the right spot. מר זוטרא answers from a פסוק that only a זריקה that permits the meat can create פיגול. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that next-day intent can still make an offering פסול, like מחשבת הינוח according to רבי יהודה. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן then give two different ways to explain our משנה. ריש לקיש says the wrong-spot blood was placed with a stated intent. רבי יוחנן says it was placed in silence and simply does not count. The משנה's words 'no כרת' remain a difficulty for רבי יוחנן. He defends himself against a second challenge by following רבי יוסי, who holds that blood placed in the wrong area may not be gathered up again.

steps.title: Wrong place makes it unfit, wrong time makes it פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states the basic contrast: intent for outside its place makes the קרבן פסול with no כרת. Intent for outside its time makes it פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to do it outside its place, the קרבן is unfit, and there is no כרת. If he intended to do it outside its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing to quote a ברייתא. This part lays out the two kinds of bad intention and their results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both bad intentions ruin the קרבן, but only intent about time creates פיגול. Only פיגול carries the punishment of כרת for someone who eats it. Intent about place makes the קרבן only פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside its place: intent to eat or offer it outside the permitted area
Outside its time: intent to eat or offer it after the permitted time
A קרבן ruined by intent about time; eating it carries כרת
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven
Unfit, disqualified

phrases.english: If he intended to do it outside its place, it is unfit,
and there is no כרת for it.
If he intended to do it outside its time, it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent for outside its place makes the קרבן פסול without כרת. Intent for outside its time makes it פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: Intent to sprinkle wrongly the next day makes it only unfit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that intent to sprinkle the blood wrongly on the next day makes the קרבן only פסול. Any later intent therefore cannot make it פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to sprinkle it the next day, it is unfit. If he then went on to have another intention, whether outside its time or outside its place, it is unfit, and there is no כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a case where the first bad intention was to sprinkle the blood the next day in the wrong spot. It rules that this makes the קרבן only פסול. Because of this, a later intention cannot turn it into פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן can become פיגול only if it would otherwise have been fit. Here the first intention already made it פסול. So the second intention, even one about time, has nothing left to ruin, and there is no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Tomorrow, the next day
He went back and had another intention

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with plain intent for 'outside its time'. Here the plan was to sprinkle late and also in the wrong spot. The wrong-spot part is what keeps it from being פיגול.

phrases.english: If he intended to sprinkle it the next day, it is unfit.
If he then went on to have another intention,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ בֵּין חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ –
phrases.english: whether outside its time or outside its place,
it is unfit, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a more complex case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent to sprinkle the blood in the wrong spot on the next day makes the קרבן only פסול. Later intentions cannot create פיגול or כרת.

steps.title: Challenge: if wrong spot counts as right spot, this should be פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that blood placed 'not in its place' counts as placed 'in its place'. If that were true, the next-day case should be פיגול, not just פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if blood placed not in its place is considered like blood placed in its place, then is this case merely unfit? It is פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack the earlier view that שלא במקומו כמקומו דמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wrong-spot sprinkling counts as proper sprinkling, then intent to sprinkle in the wrong spot tomorrow equals intent to sprinkle properly tomorrow. That is classic intent outside its time, which should make the קרבן פיגול. Yet the ברייתא says only פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its place: blood put on the wrong part of the מזבח
Is considered as if in its place

phrases.english: But if blood placed not in its place
is considered like blood placed in its place,
is this case merely unfit?!
It is פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of step 2 to challenge the view that wrong-spot blood counts as right-spot blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that blood placed 'not in its place' counts as placed 'in its place'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wrong-spot sprinkling counts as proper, intent to do it tomorrow is intent outside its time, which should make it פיגול. The ברייתא instead says it is only פסול.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: Only a sprinkling that permits the meat creates פיגול
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that only a זריקה that permits the meat to be eaten can create פיגול. Wrong-spot sprinkling never permits the meat, so the case stays only פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: A sprinkling that permits the meat to be eaten can bring the קרבן to פיגול. A sprinkling that does not permit the meat to be eaten cannot bring it to פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends the view that wrong-spot blood counts. He shows that the ברייתא does not contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if wrong-spot blood counts for the owner's atonement, it does not permit the meat to be eaten. פיגול only comes through intent about a זריקה that would permit the meat. So intent to sprinkle in the wrong spot, even late, cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Permits the meat to be eaten
Brings it to the status of פיגול

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול only comes through intent about a זריקה that would actually permit the meat. Blood placed in the wrong spot may count for atonement, but it never permits the meat, so it cannot create פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This separates two jobs of the blood: bringing atonement and permitting the meat. Only the second is connected to פיגול.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
A sprinkling that permits the meat to be eaten
can bring it to פיגול;
a sprinkling that does not permit the meat to be eaten
cannot bring it to פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: זְרִיקָה דְּשָׁרְיָא בָּשָׂר בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a condition for פיגול that the case in the ברייתא does not meet.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since wrong-spot blood counts as proper, intent to sprinkle it late should be פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wrong-spot blood may count for atonement, but it does not permit the meat. Only a זריקה that permits the meat can create פיגול.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for the source of מר זוטרא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא where he learns that only a זריקה that permits the meat can create פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא for the source of his rule from the last step. This question sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא's answer in step 4 sounded like a logical rule. רב אשי wants to know if it has a basis in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? (a request for a source)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra:
From where do you have this?
phrases.notes: "This" means מר זוטרא's rule from step 4: only a זריקה that permits the meat can make פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: מְנָא לָךְ הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the answer given in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that only a זריקה that permits the meat can create פיגול.

steps.title: The source: פיגול only when the פיגול intent alone caused it
steps.stepSummary: The answer quotes the פסוק about פיגול. It reads it to mean that פיגול applies only when the פיגול intent by itself caused the problem, not when a different flaw is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And if any of the flesh of his peace offering is eaten... it shall be פיגול." This refers to one whose פיגול caused it. Excluded is this case, where its פיגול did not cause it. Instead, the prohibition of something else caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to רב אשי is a פסוק about שלמים eaten on the third day. The פסוק is read to say that פיגול applies only when the next-day intent alone is the cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case there are two problems: the blood is put in the wrong spot, and there is intent for the next day. The wrong spot is already a flaw on its own, so the פיגול intent is not the only cause. That is why the פסוק leaves this case out of פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall be פיגול" (the פסוק that is the source for פיגול)
Its פיגול intent is what caused it
A different prohibition, meaning a separate flaw
This case is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול only happens when the time-intent alone is what ruins the offering. If a separate flaw is already involved, there is no פיגול.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And if it is eaten at all
of the flesh of his peace offering...
it shall be פיגול":
meaning one whose פיגול caused it;

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה – שֶׁאֵין פִּיגּוּלוֹ גָּרַם לוֹ,
phrases.english: this one is excluded, where its פיגול did not cause it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לוֹ.
phrases.english: rather the prohibition of something else caused it.
phrases.notes: The "something else" is putting the blood in the wrong spot.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאִם הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל מִבְּשַׂר זֶבַח שְׁלָמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question by giving the source from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 7:18 teaches that פיגול applies only when the פיגול intent alone caused the problem. Wrong-spot sprinkling brings in a separate flaw, so it is excluded.

steps.title: Then why is the offering disqualified at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the next-day intent does not count here, the offering should not even be פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should not even be disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If the next-day intent is pushed aside and does not make פיגול, why does it make the offering פסול?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view under discussion holds that wrong-spot blood counts as if it were put in the right spot. So the wrong spot alone does not ruin it. If the next-day intent also does nothing, nothing is left to make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from the previous logic)
It should not even be disqualified

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אִיפְּסוֹלֵי נָמֵי לָא לִיפְּסֵל!
phrases.english: If so, it should not even be disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אִיפְּסוֹלֵי נָמֵי לָא לִיפְּסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of the answer just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the offering is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wrong-spot blood counts as proper and the next-day intent cannot make פיגול, there is no reason left for the offering to be פסול.

steps.title: Like the intent to leave the blood, per רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that next-day intent can make an offering פסול even without making it פיגול. This is like מחשבת הינוח according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is just like the intent of leaving over, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by pointing to a known case. In that case, intent about the next day makes the offering פסול but not פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, intent to leave the blood until tomorrow disqualifies the offering even though it is not פיגול. So our case can work the same way: no פיגול, but still פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like (introduces a comparison)
The intent to leave part of the offering over until the next day
According to the opinion of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is just like the intent of leaving over,
phrases.notes: He means intent to leave the blood for tomorrow instead of putting it on the מזבח. This case comes up in the next פרק.

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּחְשֶׁבֶת הִינּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by bringing a parallel case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (מידי דהוה, a known ruling)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If intent does not make פיגול, it should have no effect at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Next-day intent can disqualify without making פיגול, as with מחשבת הינוח according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a middle level: some next-day intents make an offering פסול without making it פיגול.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: truly disqualified, yet wrong spot normally counts
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the פסול in the משנה is literal and the owner gets no atonement. Yet he also holds that blood put in the wrong spot counts as if it were put in the right spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Actually, it is literally disqualified. And blood put not in its place is considered like it was put in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a different approach. He makes two claims that seem to clash, and the next step will explain how they fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Literally פסול" means no כפרה at all. But "wrong spot counts as right spot" suggests the blood does work. Saying both at once raises an obvious question, which he answers next.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually (introduces the true position)
Literally disqualified, with no atonement at all
Blood put in the wrong place counts as if put in the right place

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Actually, it is literally disqualified,
phrases.notes: He means truly פסול: the owner does not even get atonement.

phrases.english: and blood not in its place is considered like in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם פָּסוּל מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a separate opinion about the משנה's ruling that misplaced blood disqualifies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's פסול is literal (no כפרה), and yet wrong-spot blood generally counts as right-spot blood.

steps.title: Silent placement versus placement with a statement
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains there is no contradiction. Wrong-spot blood placed in silence counts. Wrong-spot blood placed with a statement of next-day intent is truly פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not difficult: here, where he placed it in silence; there, where he placed it with a statement.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש settles the clash between his two claims by splitting into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן puts the blood in the wrong spot with no special intent, it counts and brings כפרה. The משנה's case is where he put it there with a statement of intent beyond its time, and then the offering is truly פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
In silence, without any special intent
With a statement, meaning with a stated intent

steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש, wrong-spot blood counts when placed in silence. With a stated next-day intent, the offering is truly פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases have blood in the wrong spot. The only difference is whether the כהן had a stated intent, not where the blood went.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult:
here, where he placed it in silence,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the rule that wrong-spot blood still counts.

phrases.english: there, where he placed it with a statement.
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה's case, where he had intent to eat it beyond its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן שֶׁנָּתַן בִּשְׁתִיקָה, כָּאן שֶׁנָּתַן בַּאֲמִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction inside ריש לקיש's own statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (אוקימתא by circumstance)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying both "truly פסול" and "wrong spot counts" seems contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: Silent wrong-spot placement counts. Placement with a stated next-day intent is truly פסול.

steps.title: The earlier challenges apply to ריש לקיש too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats, in short form, the earlier ברייתא challenge and its answers, now aimed at ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he intended to place blood meant for below the line above it, or blood meant for above the line below it, and so on, until the answer 'just like intent to leave over, according to רבי יהודה,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that ריש לקיש agrees that wrong-spot blood counts. So the whole earlier discussion applies to him: the ברייתא (steps 1–2), the challenge (step 3), and the answers (steps 4–8). The גמרא only quotes its first and last words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The גמרא is simply moving the whole earlier debate over to ריש לקיש. It ends at the same answer: next-day intent can make an offering פסול without making it פיגול, like מחשבת הינוח according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He had in mind (intended)
Blood meant to be placed below the red line of the מזבח
'Until': the discussion runs up to this point
'Etc.': the rest is skipped because it was already said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new question. It is the same earlier discussion, quoted by its first and last words, now pointed at ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: We learned: if he intended to place
the blood meant for below, above;
or the blood meant for above, below
until: 'just like the intent to leave over'
phrases.notes: Read this as 'repeat everything from before, up to this answer.'

phrases.english: 'and according to רבי יהודה,' etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: חִישֵּׁב לִיתֵּן אֶת הַנִּיתָּנִין לְמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the earlier challenge-and-answer cycle over to ריש לקיש, whose view was set out in steps 9–10.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that wrong-spot blood counts as if it were in the right spot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא that challenged the earlier view challenges ריש לקיש too, and the same answers rescue him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's different explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says both משניות deal with blood placed in silence. Wrong-spot blood does not count. The difference is whether lifeblood is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: in both cases he placed the blood in silence, and blood in the wrong spot is not like blood in its right spot. This one is where there is still lifeblood left, and that one is where there is no lifeblood left.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new way to explain our משנה, different from ריש לקיש. In his view nobody said anything at all, and wrong-spot blood simply does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש needed spoken next-day intent to explain why the offering is פסול. רבי יוחנן needs no intent at all, because for him wrong-spot blood is worthless. The other משנה lets him place the blood again only because more lifeblood is still available. In our משנה there is none left, so the offering stays פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
In silence, with no stated intent
Not in its proper place
Is not considered as if it were in its proper place
Lifeblood: the blood that flows out at slaughter, which is fit for the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן: does blood placed in the wrong spot count, or is it worthless?

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
Both this and that are where he placed it in silence,
phrases.notes: 'Both' means our משנה and the משנה in the next chapter, which lets him collect the blood and place it again.

phrases.english: and blood not in its place is not considered as if in its place.
And that one is where there is still lifeblood,
this one is where there is no lifeblood left.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי שֶׁנָּתַן בִּשְׁתִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to ריש לקיש's way of explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood placed in the wrong spot, even in silence, does not count. The offering can be fixed only if more lifeblood remains.

steps.title: Why would the משנה say 'no כרת'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's words 'אין בו כרת' fit ריש לקיש well but seem pointless for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: it is פסול and there is no כרת. That makes sense for ריש לקיש, which is why it says 'פסול and no כרת.' But for רבי יוחנן, what is the point of saying 'no כרת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the person did state פיגול-type intent. So the משנה has to tell us that it still does not become פיגול and there is no כרת. For רבי יוחנן, nothing was said at all, so nobody would ever think of כרת, and the phrase seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, the punishment for eating פיגול
Granted, this works well for...
That is why it teaches...
But (introducing the side that has the problem)

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה deals with blood placed in silence
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without any פיגול intent, nobody would think of כרת, so the משנה's phrase 'no כרת' would be pointless.

steps.title: The question stands against רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the challenge is not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this line by admitting it has no answer for רבי יוחנן on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the challenge stays standing. It does not mean רבי יוחנן's view is thrown out completely. It means the משנה's wording fits ריש לקיש better.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says spoken next-day intent makes the offering פסול without making it פיגול, which explains 'no כרת.' רבי יוחנן says wrong-spot blood never counts, but then the משנה's 'no כרת' is hard for him.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא.' It leaves a difficulty open but does not fully reject the opinion.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 13 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The phrase 'אין בו כרת' remains a difficulty for רבי יוחנן's explanation.

steps.title: What do the words 'no כרת' mean for שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה's phrase 'אין בו כרת' means according to שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, what does 'there is no כרת in it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after showing that these words are a problem for רבי יוחנן, the גמרא asks how שמואל explains the same words. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא's reading of the משנה has to explain every phrase in it. The phrase 'אין בו כרת' seemed to have no purpose under רבי יוחנן's reading, so now the גמרא checks whether שמואל's reading can give it a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול
What? What is meant by?

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, what is the meaning of 'there is no כרת in it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies to שמואל the same wording test that רבי יוחנן could not pass
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every phrase in the משנה must have a purpose. The question is what purpose 'אין בו כרת' has under שמואל's view.

steps.title: שמואל: the words refer to placing the blood with intent
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that if the blood was placed with a פיגול-type intention, the offering is פסול but carries no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: if he placed the blood with intent, it is פסול, but there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל by reading the phrase as describing a specific case: blood placed in the wrong spot while thinking a disqualifying thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, 'אין בו כרת' teaches a real חידוש. A wrong-spot placement together with a disqualifying intention ruins the offering. But it does not create full פיגול with כרת, because a placement like that could never have made the meat permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say

phrases.english: it is disqualified, but there is no כרת in it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the phrase as referring to a particular case (placement with intent)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase might seem to have no purpose, just as it seemed for רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: For שמואל, the phrase teaches that placement with intent makes the offering פסול without כרת
steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל, 'אין בו כרת' has a real job: wrong-spot placement with intent makes the offering פסול but not פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: For רבי יוחנן, why not gather the blood up again?
steps.stepSummary: If wrong-spot blood does not count, it should be like blood spilled on the floor, which can be gathered up and placed properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יוחנן: if blood placed in the wrong spot is not like blood in its proper spot, then it should be like blood that spilled from the vessel onto the floor, and he should gather it up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן from a new angle. If wrong-spot blood simply doesn't count, why does the משנה call the offering פסול instead of letting the כהן fix it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spilled blood is not lost, because the כהן can scoop it up and do the עבודה again. If רבי יוחנן says wrong-spot blood is 'nothing', it should work the same way. So the משנה should not rule the offering פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a fresh challenge against רבי יוחנן after the wording discussion ends
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that wrong-spot blood does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wrong-spot blood is 'nothing', it should be treated like spilled blood, which can be recovered. Then the משנה should not rule the offering פסול.

steps.title: The משנה follows the view that he may not gather it up
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the משנה holds like the opinion that wrong-spot blood may not be gathered up again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the one who says: he may not gather it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is an opinion that blood placed in the wrong spot cannot be gathered up and used again, and the משנה follows that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong-spot blood does not count as a proper placement. Still, it is not exactly like spilled blood, because by one opinion it can no longer be recovered. So the offering stays פסול, which fits רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: He holds like the one who says: he may not gather it up.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of our משנה. The next step shows this is רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: Source: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue about gathering it up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that everyone agrees blood placed in the right area but in the wrong way cannot be gathered up. When blood was placed in the wrong area (above instead of below, or below instead of above), רבי יוסי says it may not be gathered up and רבי שמעון says it may.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that blood meant for above that was placed above, or meant for below that was placed below, but not in the way its מצוה requires, may not be gathered up. They only argue about blood meant for above that was placed below, or meant for below that was placed above. רבי יוסי says he may not gather it up, and רבי שמעון says he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a source to prove that the view 'he may not gather it up' really exists. It is רבי יוסי's view in a מחלוקת with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching separates two cases. In the first, the blood reached the right area but in a wrong way, and everyone agrees it cannot be gathered up. In the second, it reached the wrong area, and that is where רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue. Our משנה is about the second case, so it follows רבי יוסי, and רבי יוחנן's reading holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Wrong area, meaning above instead of below or the reverse, is a מחלוקת: רבי יוסי says it may not be gathered up, and רבי שמעון says it may. Our משנה, as רבי יוחנן reads it, follows רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'Not as its מצוה requires' means the right area done the wrong way, and everyone agrees there. The מחלוקת is only about the wrong area.
